research_question: What is the effect of a higher blood pressure target compared with a lower blood pressure target on all-cause mortality in older adults with hypertension?
outcome_description: All-cause mortality, defined as death from any cause occurring during the trial follow-up period.
positive_direction: Reduced all-cause mortality, favoring the higher blood pressure target arm.
search_queries: higher blood pressure target lower target hypertension trial mortality
blood pressure targets older adults hypertension randomized trial all-cause mortality
systolic blood pressure target comparison trial hypertension mortality outcome
inclusion_criteria: Randomized controlled trials or comparative clinical studies evaluating higher versus lower blood pressure targets in adults (particularly older adults) with hypertension.
Studies reporting quantitative counts of all-cause mortality (deaths from any cause) and total participants randomized in both treatment arms.
exclusion_criteria: Not an original empirical study (systematic reviews, meta-analyses, narrative reviews, editorials, commentaries, conference abstracts without full quantitative data, and theoretical papers).
No comparison between a higher blood pressure target arm and a lower blood pressure target arm.
No quantitative data on all-cause mortality (number of deaths and sample size per arm missing or unextractable).
Completely unrelated to blood pressure target interventions or hypertension management.
moderators_to_extract: Mean age of participants or older-adult age threshold (e.g., >=65 vs >=75 years)
Specific target systolic/diastolic blood pressure values per arm
Achieved systolic/diastolic blood pressure difference between arms
Baseline prevalence of cardiovascular disease or diabetes
effect_size_note: Dichotomous event data (deaths / total randomized per arm) pooled as Risk Ratio (RR). An RR < 1 indicates a lower risk of all-cause mortality in the higher blood pressure target arm compared with the lower target arm.
